title: Sharp ATE Bounds from Fixed-Size Cluster Counts in Hierarchical Causal Models

tldr: Fixed-size cluster counts reveal only degree-\(m\) Bernstein moments of latent four-cell exposure--outcome laws, so the cluster-equally-weighted ATE is generally an interval rather than a point. Each hierarchical SCM carries \(\mu\in\mathcal P(K_{\epsilon})\), draws \(Q_i\sim\mu\), and calibrates the observed four-cell law to \(Q_i\). For every relative-interior count law, the sharp interval has attained generalized-moment primal and Bernstein-polynomial dual programs, with compatible endpoint SCMs using at most \({m+3\choose3}\) latent laws. Its worst-case width is \(2d_m(\epsilon)\), and the shifted-Chebyshev construction gives \(0<d_m(\epsilon)\leq\operatorname{sech}(m\operatorname{arcosh}(1/(1-2\epsilon)))\leq(1-2\epsilon)^m\), with the last inequality strict for \(m\geq2\). A generic contact-hull theorem characterizes equality with valid degree-\(m\) count-measurable envelopes and gives strict improvement regions. Exact multinomial likelihood inversion yields a semialgebraic ATE confidence set recoverable by terminating CAD, and the entire relative boundary admits a finite truth-invariant semialgebraic stratification with constant identification-dimension and minimum endpoint-support labels.
gap: The São Paulo DOT analysis shows that city random-effect choices move the posterior ATE, while fixed-plate mixture theory establishes finite-moment information loss without characterizing this causal functional. Existing limited-pooling ATE bounds use particular valid polynomials, and generalized-moment theory lacks the hierarchical SCM semantics and strict-fiber conclusion.
fill: The paper derives the sharp primal--dual interval, proves an iff Bernstein-span identification frontier and strict width throughout the relative interior, constructs finite-latent endpoint SCMs, gives an exact contact-hull criterion and strict improvement regions for every valid degree-\(m\) envelope with Lee--Weidner as a corollary, and turns exact multinomial inversion into a one-dimensional semialgebraic confidence set with terminating CAD recovery.
